title: On the Optimality of Mental Accounting
abstract: arXiv:2610.12587v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Mental accounting is usually explained by self-control, and two-stage budgeting by separable preferences. We propose a third explanation based on sellers' market power. A consumer who commits to spend a fixed number of dollars in a category has unit-elastic demand, so a seller in that category gains nothing by restricting quantity. A consumer who instead targets a fixed physical quantity has perfectly inelastic demand, a case that a monopolist can exploit. We characterize the commitments that remove a seller's incentive to mark up prices, and show that the fixed dollar budget is the least restrictive. We then show that what matters is budget rigidity rather than separability of preferences. A consumer who re-optimizes her category budget when prices change is insulated from market power only if categories are substitutes; a rigid budget insulates her in every case. translated_abstract: 心理账户通常用自我控制来解释，两阶段预算则用可分离偏好来解释。我们提出了基于卖方市场势力的第三种解释。承诺在某一消费类别中花费固定金额的消费者具有单位弹性需求，因此该类别的卖方通过限制数量无法获得任何好处。相反，以固定实物数量为目标的消费者则具有完全无弹性需求，这正是垄断者可以利用的情形。我们刻画了能够消除卖方加价激励的各类承诺方式，并证明固定美元预算是限制性最小的一种。我们随后表明，真正起作用的是预算的刚性，而非偏好的可分离性。当价格变化时重新优化其类别预算的消费者，只有在各类别互为替代品时才能免受市场势力的影响；而刚性预算在任何情况下都能保护她。因此，心理账户可以被解读为一种对抗市场势力的承诺装置。
tldr: 本文提出心理账户（固定美元预算）可被视为消费者对抗卖方市场势力的最优承诺装置，因为单位弹性需求消除了卖方限制数量和加价的激励，且起关键作用的是预算刚性而非偏好可分离性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes that mental accounting (a fixed dollar budget) is an optimal commitment device against sellers' market power, since unit-elastic demand removes sellers' incentive to restrict quantity or mark up prices, and budget rigidity—rather than preference separability—is what truly matters.
